channel.title: NeuraFeed news desk (verified stories)
channel.description: AI news stories the NeuraFeed desk checked against at least two sources. Summaries use only facts from those sources.

item.title: Anthropic is about to spend another $45 billion on AI computing power
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Bloomberg reports Anthropic is in talks to buy about $45 billion in computing power from Nscale, an Nvidia backed AI cloud company. It would be the second deal of roughly that size between the two in two months. Sources say it could close within days, though terms could change. The new capacity would come from a second building at Nscale's Monarch campus in West Virginia, with about 460 megawatts of Nvidia's next generation Vera Rubin chips. Sources: Bloomberg via Investing.com, Crypto Briefing, Finimize.

item.title: Meta's AI supercomputer in Ohio is racing toward 1 million GPUs
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Meta says Prometheus in New Albany, Ohio, already runs hundreds of thousands of GPUs across several connected buildings. Its first phase is done. That phase trained Meta's Muse models, including Muse Wonder. Two years ago the site was a regular data center serving web traffic. In mid 2025, Meta saw nearly 1,000 interruptions per day for every 8,000 GPUs. One failed part can stall a giant training job. Meta says it has cut that rate by 99 percent. Its goal is just two interruptions per 8,000 GPUs per day. Sources: Engineering at Meta, StorageReview, Unite.AI.

item.title: One hacker let AI agents break into 100+ company websites. Each hack cost about $50
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: A Chinese-speaking hacker used AI agents to break into the websites of more than 100 companies, Reuters reports. Named victims include Deere, SharkNinja and Cummins. Deere says it saw no sign sensitive information was accessed. SharkNinja says only a standalone support site was hit and the threat was contained. The attacker used Cairn, an open source platform that takes a target and a goal and sets AI agents to work on it step by step. Sources: Reuters, The Next Web, PYMNTS, IBTimes UK.

item.title: Elon Musk just promised a SpaceX share to every kid in America
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: On Monday, Musk wrote on X: "Next year, I will give one of my SpaceX shares to every kid in America. This will be the first of many." There are just over 72 million people under 18 in the U.S., according to Census Bureau figures cited by Axios. SpaceX shares closed at $146.03 on Friday. At that price, one share per child adds up to a little over $10.5 billion. Musk owns billions of SpaceX shares, so Axios notes the giveaway would barely dent his stake. Sources: Axios, The National Desk (with AP), The Decoder, Fox Business, Elon Musk on X.

item.title: The OpenAI bugging suspect was texting a Saudi royal days before his arrest, feds say
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Prosecutors say Abdulrahman Alfozan, the former OpenAI engineer accused of bugging an executive conference room, was in frequent WhatsApp contact with a Saudi royal in 2025 and 2026. The royal is not named. Their most recent contact was on October 5, four days before his arrest. The filing says the royal tried to recruit him to an AI initiative in Saudi Arabia. Alfozan allegedly agreed, but said he would not leave OpenAI until his stock vested. Prosecutors do not say the royal directed the device or any theft of information. Sources: CNBC, Quartz, NewsBytes.

item.title: Elon Musk tells Anthropic to give its shares directly to the public, says he'll do it too
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Anthropic announced Sunday it will commit 5% of its shares to a new Anthropic Public Benefit Fund. Musk answered on X: "I recommend giving the shares directly to the public." In a follow-up post he added: "This is what I will be doing." He gave no details on which shares, who gets them or when. The plan still needs stockholder approval. The board can add 2% more shares for every 50% rise in Anthropic's value above a baseline it has not disclosed. Sources: Benzinga via Yahoo Finance, The Hans India, Free Press Journal, Anthropic, The Hill.

item.title: Meta just blamed Claude for knocking a protest group off Instagram
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: The No Kings Coalition's Instagram account went dark around 1:30 p.m. Eastern on Oct. 17, during a day of action with nearly 3,000 planned events. Public access came back about 90 minutes later. Organizers say it took hours more before they could manage the account again. Meta says a tool built on Anthropic's Claude was reading Instagram profiles, posts and hashtags at about four times the normal rate, in intense bursts. Sources: The Straits Times via Red Hot Singapore, Startup Fortune, Crypto Briefing, TokenPost.
item.category: The Straits Times via Red Hot Singapore

item.title: Anthropic just pledged $48 billion in stock to a fund that grows as the company grows
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Anthropic announced Sunday that it will commit 5% of its shares to a new Anthropic Public Benefit Fund, subject to stockholder approval. Business Insider valued that stake at about $48 billion, based on Anthropic's most recent valuation. The board can add 2% more shares for every 50% increase in Anthropic's value above a set baseline, which has not been disclosed. Anthropic says it will share details on the fund's governance, structure and valuation milestones in the coming months. Sources: Anthropic, Reuters via Yahoo Finance, Business Insider via Yahoo Finance, Unite.AI.

item.title: AI could soon haggle over your salary. Anthropic is asking lawyers how to make it fair
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Anthropic has been consulting law firms on how AI agents should negotiate for users, the Financial Times reported, citing two people familiar with the talks. The deals could include haggling over product prices, settling customer service complaints and pushing for better salary offers. One open question is how often an agent should check back with its human in the middle of a deal. Another is how suspicious it should be of the AI on the other side without becoming "paranoid" or slipping into "conspiratorial thinking." Sources: PYMNTS, The Decoder, AI Weekly, NewsBytes.

item.title: Sam Altman says OpenAI will build a humanoid robot. He expects a demo in 2027
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: On the Sources podcast, Altman was asked if OpenAI would build a humanoid robot. His answer: "We will." He said the human shape makes sense because "the world is very much designed for people," so "matching that form factor seems good." Altman says the robot's looks are "less important than really figuring out ... the brain that makes the robot work." OpenAI has tried robotics before. Its Dactyl project trained a robot hand in simulation, and the same approach was later used to solve a Rubik's Cube. Sources: Engadget, Tbreak, dev.ua (citing Fortune), BigGo Finance.

item.title: Hackers just got into OpenCode and may have your OpenAI and Claude keys
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: OpenCode, an open source AI coding platform, says someone gained unauthorized access to a legacy system it was in the process of shutting down. It emailed affected users on Saturday, October 17. Users who did not get an email were not affected, the company says. About 1.4% of Console users who linked outside AI providers are in scope. Their stored OpenAI, Anthropic and Google API keys may have been exposed. Sources: Cybersecurity News, Dealroom, Crypto Briefing, Blockonomi.

item.title: ChatGPT now builds your slide deck, and your whole team can edit it live
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: OpenAI started rolling out ChatGPT Slides on October 16. It builds a presentation from a conversation, uploaded files or an outline. You can also hand it an example deck, and it follows that deck's style and layout. Change text, images, shapes and charts directly, or just tell ChatGPT what to fix. You can generate custom images or add your own. On mobile you can create slides through chat and view decks, but not edit each element directly. Sources: Superpower Daily, Tech Journal, Kaizen AI Consulting, Digital Today.
